Application Information
The application for Fall 2027 admission will open on October 1, 2026. Please refer to this site for the most current application information.
Application deadlines for Master’s and PhD programs are listed in the admissions calendar below.
The Graduate Division uses SLATE, an online application system. You are advised to check your individual graduate group for specialized requirements and deadlines. Please check their individual websites.
For guidance regarding AI usage in application materials please refer to AI Use in the Admissions Process.
Required application materials:
Online application form
Application fee payment ($90) or approval of Application Fee Waiver Request (instructions to complete form below).
Transcripts uploaded to the application
Letters of recommendation
Statement of purpose
GRE, where required. Check your graduate group for details on program requirements.
Demonstration of English proficiency, where required
Writing sample, where required
The Graduate Division may request additional academic documents, as needed.
You may access your application to update or change information until you submit the application to us. You can only submit one application to one program within the same school. Once your application has been submitted, you will be able to check its status and note the receipt of supporting documentation. It is not necessary for recommendation letters before you submit. You should submit as soon as you are finished and before the deadline.
It is important that applicants continue to check on the status of their applications until all supporting materials have been received. In order to expedite the review of your materials, we strongly suggest that you take advantage of the option to scan unofficial copies of your transcript. An official final copy of your transcript will be requested when you have been admitted and should be sent to this office.
If you have questions about the application process, please email sas-gradadmissions@sas.upenn.edu.
Apply here
Be advised that most admissions decisions for the PhD degree are made in the Spring. Admission decisions are made by individual graduate groups. The official acceptance letter is generated by the Office of the Graduate Division of Arts and Sciences, although students may also receive a separate letter from the chair of the graduate group.

Please note, most graduate groups do not offer Spring admission for PhD or Masters programs. For detailed information regarding your area of interest, please reach out directly to the graduate program.
All applications for graduate programs in SAS must be submitted electronically only.

Application Fee Waiver Request Form
A limited number of application fee waivers are available for Ph.D. applicants who demonstrate clear and compelling financial hardship. Waivers are managed exclusively by the Graduate Division of the School of Arts and Sciences.
To request a waiver or to apply a specific code given to you by a representative, begin your application after it opens on October 1st. The request form and instructions are included in the application.
If you are requesting a waiver, you should select “Request an Application Fee Waiver” at the top of the form.
If you have been instructed to use a specific code, you should select “Enter a Fee Waiver Code” at the top of the form.
Waiver requests will not be reviewed until your application has been finalized*. Requests are reviewed manually and generally require at least 7-14 business days to receive a decision. Please do not pay the application fee while waiting for your request to be reviewed, the fee is non-refundable once paid. You will be notified automatically by email once a decision is made.
Due to the volume of requests received, if requesting a waiver, please finalize your application and submit your waiver request at least 2 weeks prior to the application deadline to allow for processing and to ensure your application is included in the review process.
If your waiver request is denied, you must pay the application fee in order to finalize your application for consideration.
If you encounter any issues, please email sas-gradadmissions@sas.upenn.edu
Personal information regarding waiver requests should not be sent directly to our office by email. Please use the designated form in the application instead.
Please be advised that the office of admissions does not provide status updates, timeline estimates, or decisions by phone or email. Do not reach out regarding the status of your request unless 14 business days have passed, and you have not received a decision.
*On finalizing the application, even if you have requested the waiver, you will see the application pay wall while your request is being reviewed. Do not pay the application fee while waiting for a waiver decision. Once paid, the fee is nonrefundable.
International Applicants
If you are applying from abroad, certain special instructions apply to you.
International students must pay the application fee using a credit card. All major credit cards are accepted.
International applicants whose native language is not English must submit proof of English proficiency  (TOEFL/IELTS) . Certain programs may waive this requirement if your post-secondary degree was conducted entirely in English.  Please contact your program of interest directly regarding their policy if you are interested in requesting a waiver during the application process. In most cases, you will be required to have uploaded a copy of your unofficial transcript to the application prior to being considered for a waiver.
Upon admission, after accepting your offer and paying the enrollment fee, your name will be forwarded to the University's International Student and Scholar Services. They will provide you with a link to their database once your acceptance has been received. All documents required for the visa process will be issued by their office. Any questions regarding the visa process should be directed to them.
A helpful site to visit during your application process is EducationUSA. This website provides information and a list of advising centers in your country that can help you begin your graduate studies in the United States.
